series.name: Northbound (citybound), Ecocounter 2013-2025
series.evidence: Ecocounter 231 ran 2013-03 to 2025-04-14; MetroCount 355 started 2025-10-11 after a 6-month gap with no overlap and reads about 35% higher (April 2025 1071/day vs April 2026 1443/day for the citybound direction). Other City of Sydney sites replaced at the same time step up similarly (Bourke St N of Thurlow +44%, Kent St +53% April-on-April) while the continuous Anzac Pde counter was about +3% year on year, so the jump is an instrument change and the counters are not comparable.

series.name: Southbound (outbound), Ecocounter 2013-2025
series.evidence: Same as northbound: 887/day in April 2025 on counter 231 vs 1212/day in April 2026 on counter 355 (+37%), matching a network-wide step at the counter replacement, so kept separate.

series.name: Citybound (labelled East), MetroCount 2025-
series.evidence: Corresponds to 322 (both citybound; the higher direction by a similar ratio of about 1.2), but the new counter reads about 35% higher, so it is its own series.

series.name: Outbound (labelled West), MetroCount 2025-
series.evidence: Corresponds to 323 (both non-citybound), but the level is not comparable across the counter replacement, so it is its own series.

summary: Bourke St (W) S of Taylor Sq has a long, clean Ecocounter record (2013-2025), with two long outages (Dec 2014 to Apr 2016 and Mar 2021 to Jan 2022) already set missing by zero_outage, and about 40 days of exact duplicate records (8 records per slot instead of 4) correctly removed by duplicate_record; no further changes are needed. The MetroCount unit that replaced it in Oct 2025 reads about 35% higher, in line with a step-up seen at other City of Sydney sites replaced at the same time, so the old and new counters are kept as separate series.
